keyFindings.description: The carry decides whose approval to write from the tree's own `state`/`answered_by`/`answered_at` attributes (askBlockStates, :159-176) and never reads the `asks` rows. Those attributes are stripped only on markdown writes (docs/tree.go:146-149 -> StripServerOwnedAttrs, its one caller). A bearer session may open the document socket (/ws/doc/{room}: api/server.go:318-322; docs/websocket.go:300-317 accepts the shared agent token with a session actor; :277-284 makes it writable on an open issue), and Yjs attributes reach the tree verbatim (pmdoc/read.go:79-86). Settlement repairs server attributes only on a block parseAskBlock accepts; a block it rejects (an empty question, ask_blocks.go:651) gets only `invalid` (ask_blocks.go:252-267) and keeps the forged attributes into the tree the same transaction versions (service.go:1374-1415, :1504). withoutAskBlocks drops every ask node, invalid ones included, so the cut comparison passes; the per-block test at :104-111 passes because the forged block names the login it supplied; latestReviewBy finds the approver's approval; docs.WriteReview writes `approved` in his name, answers any open request `Approve` in his name, and the daemon opens the design gate (classify/decisions.go:360-377 reads no actor). Traced at every link in code; not driven against a running server. Fix: resolve the newly answered block's state and answerer from the `asks` rows the settlement already loads and locks (loadAskBlocks), and refuse to carry when the new version holds any ask node no row of this document backs (a copy included) or that carries `invalid`.

The browser cut is lexical and reads inside code: a fenced ```markdown example holding `:::ask{...}` ... `:::` has its body cut, while the server's tree cut keeps the code block verbatim. Driven at the head: cutDecisionBlocks of two versions differing only inside such an example returns equal text, so the approver's Show diff shows no change for an edit the server correctly stales on. Fix: skip fenced (``` / ~~~) and indented code while scanning, add a shared fixture with a fenced example to packages/contracts/fixtures/decision-blocks so both cuts are pinned on it.

The per-block test accepts a copied block (copied_from set) added since the approved version when its source's answerer is the approver, while holdsAnsweredBlock and newlyAnsweredBlocks treat copies as nobody's decision in this document (the PR's own test comment, api/approval_carry_test.go:665-667). An agent can plant a copy of the approver's answered block from another document of the same owner and it rides into the carried version unread. A row-backed per-block test (finding 1) closes this: a copy has no row of its own in this document.

renderWithoutAskBlocks(nil) dereferences node.Type; storedVersionTree returns (nil, true, nil) for a version below 1. Unreachable today since both review writers refuse version 0, but askBlockStates handles nil and this sibling does not. Fast-follow with the hardening below.

answerApprovalAsk updates the ask row by id alone; the human route's transition locks and re-checks the open state. Safe today under OpenApprovalAsk's `for no key update ... state = 'open'` and the owner-row lock; add `and state = 'open'` so the two writers cannot disagree on the precondition. Fast-follow.
